title: Coefficient-tower coherence of the specified quotient-completion exchange
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R\xrightarrow a S\xrightarrow b V$ be homomorphisms of sheaves of commutative rings. Assume $S$ is finite free as an $R$-module sheaf and $V$ finite free as an $S$-module sheaf (ranks may be zero). Let $t\in R(1)$, $v\in S(1)$ and $w\in V(1)$ act injectively on their respective rings, with $a(t)=u v^e$ and $b(v)=z w^f$, where $u,z$ are units and $e,f\geq1$. Assume countable products of $R$-, $S$-, $V$-modules and of abelian sheaves are exact. Use the unbounded derived module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the derived scalar functors $T_a=-\otimes_R^L S$, $T_b=-\otimes_S^L V$, $T_{ba}=-\otimes_R^L V$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and the balanced scalar associator $\alpha:T_bT_a\xrightarrow\sim T_{ba}$, induced by $((p\otimes s)\otimes q)\mapsto p\otimes b(s)q$. For $A=R,S,V$ and $h=t,v,w$ respectively put
$$C_AQ=R\lim_{n\geq1}(Q\otimes_A^L A/h^nA),$$
using the strict quotient tower and its quotient augmentation $\eta^A$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. For each of $a,b,ba$, let $\epsilon$ be precisely the exchange isomorphism of [lem-pur-finite-free-completion-exchange]: the canonical tensor/product map, followed by quotient tensor associativity and the inverse of the selected-coordinate/weighted-block arithmetic-subsequence Roos map of [lem-pur-compact-support-roos-cofinality]. For $ba$ use exponent $ef$, since $(ba)(t)=b(u)z^e w^{ef}$.
Then for every $Q\in D(R)$ the following equality holds in $D(V)$, naturally in $Q$:
$$C_V(\alpha_Q)\circ\epsilon^b_{T_aQ}\circ T_b(\epsilon^a_Q)=\epsilon^{ba}_Q\circ\alpha_{C_RQ}.$$
Thus both routes from $T_bT_aC_RQ$ to $C_VT_{ba}Q$ agree for the specified maps, including their quotient augmentations. For the identity map of any one of these ring sheaves, with the same chosen section and exponent $1$, the exchange is the identity on $C_AQ$ under the scalar multiplication identification $Q\otimes_A^LA\cong Q$. After composing with the specified arithmetic restriction quasi-isomorphisms, the tower equation is represented by equality of the actual maps on both Roos product coordinates. The displayed equality therefore also holds under the normalized strict-derived-limit comparisons [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. No completeness, constructibility, boundedness or perfectness hypothesis on $Q$ is imposed.

proof.text: Reuse both the ordinary and derived scalar associators and the balanced formula from the ringed K-flat word comparison API. Their normalized formula on termwise flat K-flat resolutions extends to every complex by naturality and cancellation of the resolution quasi-isomorphism. The finite-free quotient comparison gives exactness of E_b, so its universal derived counit is invertible on every complex.

On a K-flat P, choose the three prescribed representatives. Apply the cochain horizontal coherence lemma to obtain restricted, the coordinate equation and arithmetic composition. Map these equations to the derived category. Naturality of the scalar counits moves inverse arithmetic maps across extension. Cancel the isomorphisms to obtain the required derived exchange equation.

The augmentation has coordinates (0, quotient family). Product projections and the representatives quotient formula show that extension preserves the selected quotient family; biproduct projections give the augmentation square. Map this square to the derived category and cancel the prescribed arithmetic quasi-isomorphism and computing counits. This proves unit preservation on K-flat representatives.

K-flat resolutions and localization extensionality extend the exchange and unit equations to all derived objects. The same cochain witnesses give RepresentativeComposition. Postcomposing the exchange equality with the normalized output isomorphism gives the last transport equation.

For identity coefficients reuse both the ordinary and derived scalar units and the pure-tensor formula from the ringed K-flat word comparison API. Extend the counit normalization from termwise flat K-flat resolutions to all complexes by naturality and cancellation. The existing identity quotient Roos normalization and cancellation give the exchange identity on K-flat complexes; resolutions extend it to all derived objects. Naturality of the scalar identification implies identity unit preservation.
